thread:
Emma S: Escalation from ACME support - their latency-threshold alert is firing repeatedly (~every 30s) even though traffic looks steady on their side. They included screenshots of the chart and the alert payload.
Emma S: Alert config pasted by customer: ```metric: http_request_duration_p95
aggregation: sliding_window
window: 60s
alignment: auto
threshold: > 250ms for 1 consecutive window
notify: slack#acme-oncall```
Alex O: got it. Can you drop tenant_id + a quick link to the dashboard and the alert rule URL? Also a sample alert webhook payload if available.
Emma S: tenant_id=acme-prod-42, dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/abc123/requests?panel=7, alert url: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/92731, payload attached in thread (see screenshot). Customer says spikes align to :00 and :30 seconds.
Alex O: looking at the alert timeline now. I see repeated sharp spikes in the computed series at 00s/30s boundaries, then zeros in between.
Tom P: FYI I rolled a perf tweak last week that changed timebucket rounding in the rollup layer: commit ABCD123 - "timebucket: round_to_nearest(30s) for ingestion batching". Might be interacting poorly with sliding_window alignment.
Priya M: if that's true it could make the numerator/denominator alignment drift for percentile calculations and cause apparent spikes when the window crosses batch boundaries. Customer-facing alerting expects minute-aligned buckets.
Alex O: Repro steps I used locally: run a synthetic steady traffic trace, ingest with batching enabled, then evaluate the alert rule. I can reproduce the spikes. Short repro: ```# synth traffic
for i in seq 1 600; do curl -s -X POST https://ingest.redwood.ai/tenant/acme -d '{"latency_ms": 120}' ; sleep 0.5; done
# evaluate rule snapshot
http GET https://internal-api.redwood.ai/tenants/acme/alerts/92731/eval?from=now-10m to=now```
Emma S: customer asked for a mitigation they can do on their side while we fix it. Any safe changes?
Tom P: two options: 1) revert the rounding change (hotfix) so ingestion uses start-of-minute floor, or 2) make alert evaluation use fixed bucket alignment (floor to minute) instead of auto/nearest. Hotfix is faster but heavier.
Priya M: for immediate customer relief recommend changing the alert's aggregation to "fixed_alignment: floor" or bump window to 2m temporarily. That reduces sensitivity to 30s jitter.
Alex O: I patched their rule in the console to use fixed_alignment=floor and widened to 120s. Monitoring for false negatives now. :eyes:
monitoring-bot: Deployment notice: rollback scheduled for service "ingest-rollup" at 1778468100 by Tom P (canary in us-west)
Tom P: I'll also prepare a targeted revert PR for ABCD123 and run a quick canary. If revert looks good we'll push to production and notify support.
Emma S: Customer confirmed after change spikes disappeared from their alert for the last 5 minutes. Thanks.
Priya M: Follow-up: we should add an integration test for alert eval alignment with different ingestion batch alignments. Assigning to eng-platform backlog.
Alex O: Created internal ticket INFRA-3281, set sev=high, assigned to Tom. ETA for hotfix: 2h. I'll keep the customer updated. :thumbsup:
Tom P: adding a small config flag to allow "prefer_fixed_alignment" default false; can flip for affected tenants quickly if we see other reports.
Emma S: Marking customer notified. Closing escalation for now; will reopen if spikes reappear.
Alex O: thanks all.
